notes.claim: Repeating a measurement can give a randomly different result each time, and averaging more of those readings generally gives a better estimate.
A measurement result is stated with an interval and a confidence level, such as 20 centimetres plus or minus 1 centimetre at the 95 percent confidence level.

sources.title: Good Practice Guide No. 11
sources.quote: random - where repeating the measurement gives a randomly different result. If so, the more measurements you make, and then average, the better estimate you generally can expect to get.

sources.title: Good Practice Guide No. 11
sources.quote: For example: We might say that the length of a certain stick measures 20 centimetres plus or minus 1 centimetre, at the 95 percent confidence level.
